chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from one of our companions, raising it (to the Imam), said:
He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who applies henna and massages with it from his head to his feet, poverty is negated from him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of applying henna and massaging the body according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from *Al-Kafi* links the physical act of applying henna and massaging the body to spiritual purification and the alleviation of poverty, reflecting the interconnection between bodily care and divine blessing. The practice is viewed not merely as cosmetic but as a means of enhancing one's appearance and dignity, thereby attracting sustenance and removing the state of neediness. This ritual underscores the importance of self-care as an act of worship and gratitude within the broader framework of Shia jurisprudence and spirituality.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from one of our companions, raising it,
‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who waxes and massages with the henna from his head to his feet, the poverty is negated from him’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from certain persons of our people in a marfu ‘ manner has said the following: “He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If one applies lime paste then rubs henna from his top to his toes, his poverty goes away.’”
